item.title: Lumumba identifies what’s fueling xenophobia
item.description: •Says Africa cannot fight poverty by turning against fellow Africans Professor Patrick Loch Otieno (PLO) Lumumba has warned that Africa’s failure to create sufficient economic opportunities is fuelling xenophobia. He urged governments to address unemployment, poverty and weak industrial development rather than blame migrants for the continent’s challenges. Lumumba, a renowned Kenyan legal scholar and public speaker, said xenophobia often thrived in societies experiencing economic hardship, where unemployment, inequality and pressure on public services encouraged citizens to regard foreigners as competitors. He spoke as the keynote speaker at the Bridge Club’s grand end-of-year event in Lagos on Thursday. In his address, titled Africa Must Not Become Foreign to Itself: Xenophobia, Pan-Africanism and the Future of African Belonging, Lumumba argued that migrants were frequently made scapegoats for economic problems arising from poor governance and weak institutions. He said: “The foreign trader, worker or entrepreneur can be arrested. The failure to create productive employment over several decades cannot be arrested at a roadblock.” According to him, African governments must look beyond the presence of migrants and examine the structural weaknesses responsible for unemployment, poverty and economic competition. He said the inability of many African countries to industrialise and create productive jobs had forced millions of young people into informal economic activities, where competition for limited opportunities could generate resentment. Lumumba observed that Africa’s economic dependence on exporting raw materials while importing finished products had contributed to the loss of employment opportunities to other economies. “We export crude oil and import refined petroleum. We export cocoa and import chocolate. We export minerals and import the machines, batteries and technologies manufactured from them,” he said. He added that the continent was effectively creating employment opportunities elsewhere while its young population continued to struggle for limited opportunities at home. The legal scholar said the appropriate response to the exploitation of migrant workers was to enforce labour laws against employers rather than encourage hostility towards foreigners. According to him, employers who engage undocumented migrants and pay them below lawful wages create resentment among local workers while benefiting from the division. “The appropriate response is not violence against the migrant. It is enforcement of labour law against the employer,” he said. Lumumba also highlighted the contradiction in Africans celebrating the achievements of their compatriots abroad while treating migrants from other African countries with hostility. He noted that Nigerians seeking opportunities in London, Kenyans travelling to Dubai, Ghanaians moving to Canada and Zimbabweans relocating to South Africa were motivated by the same desire to improve their living conditio

item.title: Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake edges Troy in final seconds for epic Class A football title win
item.description: Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake celebrates after beating Troy for the Section 2, Class A title on Friday, Nov. 13, 2026, at Colonie High School in Colonie, NY. (Jim Franco/Times Union) (Jim Franco/Times Union) COLONIE - The waning stages of the fourth quarter Friday night for the Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake football team were looking painfully dire, as the Spartans found themselves down a point against Troy and forced to give the ball back on a punt. In a span of a few minutes, BH-BL senior standout Login Tomlinson made two of the biggest plays of his career - the first with his hand and the second with his foot - to flip things back in favor of his team in the Section 2 Class A Super Bowl. First, Tomlinson forced Troy junior quarterback Kyair Carr to fumble the ball away at the Flying Horses' 23-yard line. Then, BH-BL had just 17 seconds left when it had Tomlinson line up for a 32-yard field goal on third down and without a timeout remaining. The senior - following a timeout by Troy - drilled a go-ahead, line-drive boot down the middle in what ended up being a thrilling 23-21 Super Bowl victory over the Flying Horses at Colonie High School. "I have been dreaming about this since I was a little kid and first starting kicking," said Tomlinson, a four-year varsity player who is headed to Siena University to play lacrosse. "It happened. It came true." "It was really nerve-racking out there," BH-BL junior quarterback Tristan West said. "I believed in him every moment when he went out there to kick." The pulse-pounding triumph secured BH-BL (11-0) the program's 11th Class A sectional title in 20 years, and first since 2021. It also marked the first championship guided by fourth-year coach Kevin DeBonis. The loss denied Troy, playing in its second straight Super Bowl, a 10th title since first winning one in 1993. "This feels amazing. Since we were little kids, this is what we have been working for," West said. Last year, the Flying Horses lost to Niskayuna. Troy senior fullback/defensive Ben Mergil, who produced two touchdown receptions and recovered a fumble by BH-BL, emerged from an emotional postgame gathering to put the defeat into context. "It is hard, but, at the end of the day, it is football," Mergil said. "Anybody that has ever played football knows it will teach life lessons. Sometimes, things just don't shake out for you, but you just have to roll with the punches. I want to thank my coaches, my teammates and God for giving me this opportunity to play for such an amazing school and play my heart out." Both squads left everything they had on the field. There were colossal swings of momentum swapped between the two teams all evening, especially down the stretch. Troy led 14-0 and went to halftime up 14-6. West connected with Michael Bies for a 21-yard touchdown pass and Owen Huggins scored on a 2-point conversion to provide BH-BL its first lead at 20-14, but Troy senior running back Nymiear Jenkins - lined up in a wildcat formation - found Mergil on a

item.title: UTSA athletics inducts fourth Hall of Fame class
item.description: From left to right, Jessica Rogers, Ryanne Dupree, Teresa Neighbors, Leonard Byrd, and Tamara Luckeymeyer were inducted as the fourth class in the UTSA Athletics Hall of Fame during a ceremony on Friday at Pedrotti's Ranch in Helotes. (Vashaun Newman/UTSA Athletics) (Vashaun Newman/UTSA Athletics) UTSA inducted three of the San Antonio area's brightest athletics stars into its 2026 Hall of Fame class during a ceremony Friday at Pedrotti's Ranch. East Central's Ryanne DuPree, Judson's Teresa Neighbors and Marshall's Leonard Byrd joined volleyball standout Tamara Luckeymeyer and softball star Jessica Rogers in UTSA's fourth Hall of Fame class. The three track and field standouts from this year's group join a list of UTSA Hall of Fame track athletes that includes Tameka Roberts-Nunez in the inaugural class as well as Starlite Williams and Teddy Williams in 2024. DuPree was a four-time All-American in the multi-events from 2004 to 2007, finishing as high as fourth in the nation and winning nine conference championships. She also holds four UTSA records, including a mark of 13.23 seconds in the 100-meter hurdles. Neighbors' third-place finish as a senior at the 1990 national championships with a mark of 6.74 seconds in the 55-meter run is tied for the highest women's NCAA Indoor individual finish in program history, setting a UTSA record that still stands. She also set then-school records in the 100 and 2000 in 1989, earning another All-America nod. Byrd was a three-time All-American in the 400-meter sprint during his time at UTSA from 1994 to 1997, finishing as high as third in the 1996 outdoor championships. He won four consecutive Southland outdoor conference titles in the event, claiming eight conference championships overall. Luckemeyer won Southland Conference Player of the Year twice in a career that spanned 1997 to 2000, helping the Roadrunners to a regular-season title in 1999 and a tournament championship in 2000. She holds the school records for kills in a career (2,034) and season (567 in 1999). Rogers was a first-team All-Southland selection in each of her four seasons from 2003 to 2007, winning the league's Player of the Year and Hitter of the Year honors in 2005. She stands as the school's career record holder for runs (159), hits (281), extra-base hits (104) and at-bats (732), and in 2005 she led the nation with 0.38 home runs per game. UTSA's Hall of Fame selection committee is made up of designees from the UTSA Alumni Association Board, Letterwinners Club, Roadrunner Foundation and Student-Athlete Advisory Committee, as well as representatives from the university and athletics department along with local print and electronic media. The Express-News was the print media representative for the first four years of the selection process. Subscribe There’s more to San Antonio with the Express-News. Subscribe today for just 25¢. item.title: 2027: Violence threatens turnout as party supporters come under attacks
item.description: •60 to 70 per cent of voters afraid of voting – security analyst •INEC warns of N10m fine, jail term for inflammatory campaigns •Attacks on rallies, convoys heighten fears By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Between 60 to 70 per cent of Nigerian voters are afraid that political violence will stop them from voting in 2027, a security expert, Mr Onyekachi Adekoya, has said, as voter apathy continues to rise. Adekoya spoke on Friday morning on The Morning Brief, a programme on Channels Television. He cited a calculation by Yiaga Africa. “If you look at Yiaga Africa’s calculation, 60 to 70% of voters are worried that political violence will not allow them come out on the day,” he said. He said that fear works against turnout. “Once the violence and the rhetoric of it goes up, people are less likely to come out to vote, and perhaps that is, some would argue, part of the strategy at play by some parties,” he said. There have been recent incidents, including attacks on party convoys and on an assembly in some states including Delta, Cross River, Lagos, Edo and Gombe states. In Delta State, a man was apprehended and not handed over to the police. He was then reportedly killed. Adekoya said violence was already rising and would get worse. “It is already ticking over 70 incidents captured so far,” he said. “This is not the peak of it because the campaign season has just started.” He said the stakes went beyond 2027, with politicians positioning for 2031 and 2039. “We expect that this political season will be a bit more violent and true to type,” he said. He said pressure on local politicians would raise tensions. “Politicians at the local level are under significant pressure to deliver on their areas and that would most likely raise tensions. What it will look like is that politicians use violence to destabilize the opponents in opponents’ area of strength so that they can lose votes.” Adekoya said his firm’s report classed 14 states as toss-up states, which would be “keenly contested”. He named the North Central, North East and North West, and parts of the South East, as areas of concern. “Nobody should die because somebody is trying to be president,” he said. On what security agencies could do, Adekoya said the shortfall lay in resources. “If at all there is a failure in security it is because of lack of capacity, poor logistics planning and the fact that we have a hydraheaded security problem which cannot be resolved,” he said. He said enforcement could not be left to the agencies alone. “There is a command structure where also politics get in the way of enforcement. It should not be a job only for the police, it should be a collective responsibility,” he said. The concerns followed a run of threats by office holders in several states in recent weeks, which has drawn condemnation from civil society groups, rights organisations and opposition politicians. item.title: Sacking of Atiku: What Justice Lifu based his judgement on
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The leadership crisis rocking the African Democratic Congress (ADC) took a decisive turn when Justice Peter Lifu of the Federal High Court, Abuja, invalidated the emergence of Senator David Mark and other executives who assumed control of the party in July 2025. But the judgment of November 5, 2026, was not simply about competing claims to party leadership. It hinged on a fundamental legal question: could the party’s National Executive Committee (NEC) use its constitutional powers to replace an existing elected leadership structure without complying with the democratic procedures prescribed by law? In the Certified True Copy (CTC) of the judgment obtained by Saturday Vanguard, Justice Lifu said he identified critical weaknesses in the defendants’ case, including the disputed resignation letter on which they relied, the limits of NEC’s administrative powers and the absence of satisfactory evidence that the new executives emerged through a democratic election. The resignation letter One of the Mark-led camp’s principal arguments was that Nafiu Bala Gombe had voluntarily resigned as Deputy National Chairman on May 17, 2025, before the NEC meeting that produced the new leadership. The letter, tendered as Exhibit ADC 1, was intended to establish that Gombe had relinquished his position and consequently lacked the legal standing to challenge the subsequent leadership transition. Justice Lifu, however, was unconvinced Rather than accept the document simply because it was certified, the judge examined its signature against Gombe’s signatures on other documents executed before a Commissioner for Oaths. He explained that certification established the status of a document as a true copy but did not, in itself, establish the authenticity of a disputed signature. After comparing the documents, he said that he found material differences in their structure, style, formation and general manner of execution. “The signatures do not appear to be one and the same,” Justice Lifu observed. He consequently described the purported resignation letter as fictitious or fabricated and rejected it as reliable evidence that Gombe had voluntarily vacated his office. The finding removed a central pillar of the defendants’ argument that Gombe had ceased to be an officer of the party before the July 2025 transition. Importantly, this was a finding made in determining the civil dispute, not a criminal conviction for forgery. NEC’s powers could not override the law The second major issue concerned the extent of NEC’s authority under Article 19(14) of the ADC constitution. The defendants maintained that the provision empowered NEC to dissolve the existing National Working Committee (NWC), make administrative arrangements and install the new executives. item.title: ‘I can’t wait’: Chad Johnson says what he’s going to do to Luka Doncic when he comes to Miami
item.description: Photo by Katelyn Mulcahy/Getty Images Former NFL star Chad ‘Ochocinco’ Johnson has continued speaking about Los Angeles Lakers superstar Luka Doncic. It all started when the 48-year-old claimed that he would lock down the Slovenian if he played in the NBA and accused other players of not watching enough film. Then, Johnson shared a screenshot of his direct message to Doncic on Instagram, challenging him to a one-on-one in June. Now, the Cincinnati Bengals legend has revealed his next plan. Chad ‘Ochocinco’ Johnson says he has bought tickets to talk trash to Luka Doncic Johnson has been taunting Doncic but has received no reply from the Los Angeles Lakers star. Yet, the former Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver has shown no willingness to stop, and his next plan is to have his say face-to-face. Ochocinco has revealed that he has bought courtside tickets for the Lakers’ game against the Miami Heat at the Kaseya Center. He says he will sit right next to the bench. He said on the Nightcap Show : “I can’t wait for him to come here. You see how I was talking trash to Anthony Edwards? Wait until the Lakers come here. “I got the same seats, Joe. You know, right next to the bench so he can see me.” Shannon Sharpe and Iso Joe Johnson both warned Ochocinco not to rile up Doncic, as it will only backfire on the Miami Heat. Joe Johnson even claimed that the Lakers star will score at least 55 points against the Heat, which would be his best return of the season. However, for any of this to happen, we have to wait a long time, as the two teams aren’t scheduled to play against each other again until March 2027. Read more: Sophie Cunningham finds Stephen A. item.title: South Africa releases Fani-Kayode’s speech after protest
item.description: South Africa’s presidency has released a separate video of Nigeria’s High Commissioner, Femi Fani-Kayode, delivering his address at a credentials presentation ceremony, hours after the diplomat protested its omission from the official livestream. Fani-Kayode had raised concerns after the live broadcast of Friday’s ceremony, at which he presented his letters of credence alongside 14 other ambassadors to South African President Cyril Ramaphosa, failed to capture his speech. The ceremony took place at the Sefako M. Makgatho Presidential Guest House in Tshwane, Gauteng, and was streamed on the South African presidency’s YouTube channel. The broadcast appeared to experience a technical interruption while French Ambassador to South Africa, Antoine Michon, was speaking. Fani-Kayode was scheduled to speak next, but the livestream cut to Ramaphosa’s address to the assembled diplomats. Reacting to the omission, Fani-Kayode suggested that his exclusion might have been deliberate, alleging that some elements in South Africa did not want to hear his views or see him. “Clearly some elements in South Africa do not want to hear what we have to say or see our faces, but we are here to stay as long as we are welcome and have the confidence of President Ramaphosa, which I am sure we do,” he said. He disclosed that he personally brought the matter to Ramaphosa’s attention during the photo session following the ceremony. According to the Nigerian envoy, the South African president took him to the relevant officials and acted promptly to address his complaint. Hours later, the presidency published a separate recording of Fani-Kayode’s speech on its YouTube channel. In the address, the Nigerian diplomat pledged to strengthen bilateral relations, particularly economic and diplomatic cooperation, between both countries. “Nothing can come between the two of us. And part of my job here is to reset that relationship, to come and build that bridge, and to ensure that whatever concerns we have mutually, we can work them out and move forward together,” he said. Recalling Nigeria’s support for South Africa during the anti-apartheid struggle, Fani-Kayode said the historical ties between both countries provided a strong foundation for closer cooperation. He described Nigeria as South Africa’s largest trading partner in Africa and stressed the importance of sustained collaboration between the two countries in advancing the continent’s interests. “Without South Africa and Nigeria working together, closely together, the destiny of our great continent may well be affected,” he said. Fani-Kayode also commended South Africa’s positions on international issues, including the conflict in Gaza, its participation in the BRICS bloc and its advocacy for the interests of the Global South. He praised Ramaphosa’s efforts towards securing Nigeria’s inclusion in the Group of 20 (G20), describing them as noteworthy and encouraging. item.title: Memorial football comes up one possession short in 3A regional championship
item.description: EVANSVILLE — Memorial coach John Hurley didn't require much time in addressing his team postgame. There wasn't much to truly say in the moment. Only one team advances at this stage. The other sat on the goal line fighting back tears in near freezing temperatures. Hurley did push across one talking point during the brief time in front of his team. This season was a success by all measures. One result in November won't diminish it. More: Southwestern Indiana regional football scores, updates Elsewhere around the area: Second half costs Castle football in Class 5A regional championship game No. 4 Indian Creek defeated No. 1 Memorial 31-28 in the Class 3A regional championship on Friday, Nov. 13 at Enlow Field. A perfect season came to a close behind early mistakes and missed opportunities. Give them one more possession in the second half, and the Tigers (12-1) are potentially playing for a spot in Lucas Oil Stadium. They just came up short. Such is football. "I give our kids a lot of credit to compete all the way up until the end," Hurley said. "It's tough to go through our conference. It's tough to go through that schedule we went from Week 7 on. We got a little bit beat up. It showed up a little bit tonight." This result boiled down to a few factors. One, Indian Creek (12-0) controlled the line of scrimmage. The Braves scored on their first two possessions of the second half and nearly bled the clock dry on a third. The offense finished with 266 rushing yards – Paxton Walters went for 109 and Patrick Dowty totaled 85 – on 49 attempts. It felt like more in the moment. Indian Creek continued to hold possession with the lead, especially a bruising drive in the fourth quarter with multiple fourth-down conversions. Quarterback Evan Clark was only asked to attempt seven passes. IC coach Max Goodin believes his team can win any number of ways – a physical push was simply the best option. "We knew we wanted to pound the rock," Goodin said. "We wanted to sustain long drives and play great defense. We really challenged our kids this week to move them up front. Pound the rock and play great defense. We feel like that's what wins championships in November." Memorial was constantly playing down multiple scores. It couldn't get Indian Creek off the field until the final minutes. The other factor was injuries finally catching up on defense. All-State linebacker Grayson Carter was a notable absence in the middle after suffering a torn ACL in the sectional semifinal. It was the most points allowed by the Tigers since 2024. "Grayson is a big deal," Hurley said. "Especially in the second half. It's a grinder going through the back end of our schedule. Hats off to Indian Creek. They did a great job. Coach Goodin has those guys playing really well. Some of those small things come and bite us back in the end." The final factor was another slow start. item.title: Husker Wrestling: #3 Nebraska Drops Friday Night Road Dual Against #2 Oklahoma State 27-6
item.description: CLEVELAND, OHIO - MARCH 21: Christopher Minto of the Nebraska Cornhuskers is introduced before his bout against Levi Haines of the Penn State Nittany Lions during the Division I Men's Wrestling Championship held at Rocket Arena on March 21, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Isaiah Vazquez/NCAA Photos via Getty Images) | NCAA Photos via Getty Images There’s no way to spin this — Nebraska got its butt kicked on Friday night. Facing the #2 Oklahoma City Cowboys, the seat right behind #1 Penn State in the national pecking order was on the line in this dual, and Oklahoma State hopped right on in there. The #3-ranked Huskers lost eight of ten matches in their 27-6 dual loss to the Cowboys. With the dual starting at 125 pounds, Nebraska lost the first six matches before returning NCAA finalist Christopher Minto finally got Nebraska on the board. As a team, Nebraska scored just two total takedowns in the dual with Minto getting the first one seven matches in. Honestly, the question all along — after the transfer portal haul by Nebraska and the two-straight monster recruiting classes by David Taylor and Oklahoma State — was whether or not Nebraska is in the same tier as Oklahoma State. Unfortunately for Nebraska, they currently are not. Here’s how it all went down. Weight-By-Weight Recap 125 pounds Nebraska’s #4 Vincent Robinson — a former national champion for NC State — took on Oklahoma State true freshman Rocklin Zinkin. A three-time California state champion, Zinkin was a big-time recruit coming out of high school. With Robinson taking the majority of the shots in regulation, the third period ended tied at 1-1, sending things to sudden victory. After a scoreless overtime period where Zinkin nearly took Robinson down late, but Robinson used his splits to ward off the points, the match went to tiebreakers. In the tiebreakers, Zinkin rode Robinson out for the full 30 seconds, forcing Robinson to choose neutral in the second tiebreaker. Robinson was unable to get through the head and hands defense of Zinkin, handing him his first loss of his Husker career 1-1 in tiebreakers. 133 pounds Facing the prodigy #1 Jax Forrest, Nebraska’s #7 Jacob Van Dee put up a valiant effort but fell in the end via 21-6 technical fall — giving the Cowboys an 8-0 dual lead. Forrest scored six takedowns, but Van Dee did score a second-period reversal — not a lot of guys score offense points on Forrest, so it’s noteworthy. After dropping his opener late and losing to Forrest, Van Dee will look for his first win this season when Nebraska travels to face #20 Penn on Nov. 21. 141 pounds In a battle of true freshmen, Oklahoma State’s prevailed with #13 Jayden Raney downing Nebraska’s Lincoln Sledzianowski 10-2 by major decision. Raney scored three takedowns in the match and earned the bonus points with a riding-time point. The Cowboy freshman was a blue-chip recruit out of high school, so this is no surprise. item.title: Naugatuck football rallies past Torrington as Qwentarvous Lee delivers two huge plays
item.description: Naugatuck's Qwentarvous Lee rushed for 133 yards, while scoring on a 78-yard fumble return and an 80-yard run in a 29-14 win over Torrington on Friday, Nov. 13, 2026, at Torrington High. (Steve Barlow/For Hearst Connecticut Media) TORRINGTON - With the annual Thanksgiving battle with Ansonia within sniffing distance, Naugatuck football coach Chris Anderson preached to his team all week long that the Greyhounds couldn't look past Torrington on Friday night. He was right. Naugy found itself trailing by a touchdown at the Robert Frost Athletic Complex, and the gap could have been even greater after another score was called back because of a false start by the Raiders. "At halftime, we told the kids, ‘Well, you've dug yourself a hole, but you've been resilient all season.' We were down to Holy Cross and Woodland, too, and won those games. We can do it again," Anderson remarked following a 29-14 victory that improved the Greyhounds to 9-0. Torrington (6-3) controlled the first half with its ball-control single-wing offense. The Raiders ran 39 plays from scrimmage, more than twice as many as Naugatuck's 17, and ate up big chunks of the clock. Torrington even held the Greyhounds scoreless in the first half for the first time all season. "Yes, we're high-powered, but when you don't have the ball, it doesn't matter," Anderson said. "When you're able to eat the clock like they can, they have the formula to beat us." Naugy, which beat Torrington on the final play each of the past two meetings, needed a big play to turn the tide. Qwentarvous Lee provided exactly that and then did it again. Ahead 8-0 after the opening half, Torrington was driving again on its first possession after intermission. But fullback Cameron Roxbury fumbled at the 22. The ball spun out of the pile to Lee, who picked it up and raced 78 yards to a touchdown. Brandon Andoh's conversion run tied the game for Naugy. "Coach put me in on defense in the second half. I noticed we weren't getting to the ball. I was driving to the ball, and all the effort paid off. The ball came out right in front of me. Josiah (Loyd) stripped it out. The ball came right to me and I took off," Lee said. Nick Coleman got the momentum right back for Torrington with a 61-yard scoring run for his second TD, but Lee immediately answered. On Naugy's next play, he burst through the line and bolted 80 yards for a touchdown. Gabriel Bello's point-after kick put his team ahead for good. "I got Llir (Mamudov) and (Logan) Washenko, two 300-pound guys, in front of me. I told them if you make your blocks and Josiah goes through and blocks the linebacker, I'm going to take off, and that's what happened," Lee said. Torrington answered by driving to the Naugy 6-yard line, but Coleman was stopped short on fourth down. "We just have to keep swarming to the ball. That was the big emphasis for the game," Loyd said. "It means a lot to get to 9-0, especially against a good team like this. They're coached well and have good athletes."

item.title: Cold weather can't cool off Purdue soccer on way to Big Ten Tournament title
item.description: WEST LAFAYETTE — It was a frigid 37 degrees on a day bogged down by rain and sleet, but adrenaline won out against the weather conditions. Purdue soccer 's Jaiden Anderson just added to her program record with her 20th goal, this one delivering a Big Ten Tournament championship in thrilling fashion. Anderson, ignoring the looming Indiana winter weather, ripped off her No. 54 jersey and ran across Folk Field twirling it above her head, was chased down from behind by teammate Emilia Deppe, who tackled Anderson to the ground as the rest of the Boilers dogpiled on top. The Big Ten's Forward of the Year had been marked by two, and sometimes three, Michigan State defenders all night before getting into the open field, juking two Spartans and ripping a shot into the lower right 90 6:35 into overtime to give Purdue a 4-3 victory. "It was just spur of the moment, pure excitement, pure love and passion for this game," Anderson said. It was the latest in a series of thrillers that brought the Boilermakers their first Big Ten Tournament championship since 2007 and the second victory this season over third-ranked Michigan State. Purdue earned its first NCAA Tournament appearance since 2021 , doing so a season after not even qualifying for the Big Ten's eight-team postseason tournament. More: 'Special team' piloting turnaround for Big Ten leading Purdue soccer Anderson's heroics were only possible after what gets lost in the post-match celebration, a diving stop by Purdue keeper Grace Miller, one of the heroes in Purdue's penalty kicks victory over Wisconsin in the Big Ten semifinals, off a Kayla Briggs header just moments earlier that briefly looked like it would have spoiled the Boilers' championship moment. Despite allowing three goals, including a game-tying boot from Mackenzie Kruer with 1:40 to go in regulation, Miller was magnificent, standing tall against a Michigan State team that dominated possession and fired 22 shots, 11 on target. Kruer's neutralized a night where goals by Rosa Maalouf, Addison Feldman and McKenzie Carle had the Boilermakers nursing a lead for nearly the duration of regulation. More: How Purdue soccer uses data to boost performance But it was the Boilermakers who capitalized most on its chances, including its final one, to assure this ride will continue at least one more week. "There's this, like, sort of chemistry on this team," Miller said. "You could see it from the sidelines and watching. Everyone is rooting for each other and I think that's what makes this team special." It was a championship performance that fell in line with a season full of thrillers. "I think this team is special," said senior midfielder Irene Campo, the tournament's Most Outstanding Player. "Everybody shows up every practice, every game. You guys have seen it today. We were up. They tied us in the last few minutes, and then we just kept pushing. We've been pushing since the first game of the season, and I think all the people that came out to see us dese

item.title: ‘Don’t Act Soft Now,’ ‘You’re Gonna Get Smoked’ — NFL Fans React to Titans HC Robert Saleh Downplaying Beef With Jaguars HC Liam Coen
item.description: ‘Don’t Act Soft Now,’ ‘You’re Gonna Get Smoked’ — NFL Fans React to Titans HC Robert Saleh Downplaying Beef With Jaguars HC Liam Coen The rivalry between Robert Saleh and Liam Coen is back in the spotlight ahead of the Week 10 showdown between the Tennessee Titans and the Jacksonville Jaguars. The two traded heated words on the field last season, but Saleh now sounds ready to bury the hatchet. He recently had kind words for Coen and the Jaguars’ coaching staff, a turn that caught NFL fans flat-footed. Fans React to Robert Saleh Squashing Beef With Liam Coen The tension between the two coaches dates back to September 2025, when Saleh was the San Francisco 49ers’ defensive coordinator. He made headlines after praising Jacksonville’s offensive preparation, describing Coen’s staff as having “legally, a really advanced signal-stealing-type system.” Coen apparently took the comment as an accusation and confronted Saleh after the Jaguars defeated the 49ers 26-21. The two coaches exchanged heated words at midfield and had to be separated. Coen was reportedly heard telling Saleh, “Keep my name out of your mouth.” What looked like the start of a bitter coaching rivalry, however, didn’t last long. Both men later said they had cleared the air at the NFL’s annual league meetings in Phoenix in March. Saleh’s comments on Friday suggest the hatchet is still buried. “Liam’s great, man,” the Titans head coach said. “We’ve had plenty of interactions. The whole thing is what it was: a little misunderstanding, poor words on my part. But they’re doing a great job. I love what they’re doing offensively. They’ve definitely got an identity. And then [defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile] on the other side. Overall, as an organization, they’ve done a really nice job.” However, Saleh’s friendly comments didn’t sit well with some NFL fans, who took to social media to criticize him for backing away from the rivalry. PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor One X user suggested Saleh was steering clear of another blowup because of Jacksonville’s current form. “He knows he’s getting belted and can’t talk crazy like he did on the Niners,” they wrote. Another fan wasn’t buying Saleh’s sudden change in tone, commenting, “Oh come on, don’t be a [expletive] now.” SET YOUR LINEUPS: PFN’s Free Fantasy Start/Sit Optimizer “Ahhhh, don’t act soft now,” another user added . Others were already counting the Jaguars’ win. One commenter put it bluntly : “Yeah, you’re gonna get smoked, buddy.” Another fan predicted a lopsided result, posting , “38-7 Jags incoming.” Meanwhile, one fan wanted the rivalry to have more bite, writing , “Man, they are acting too nice. I wanted them to hate each other like the NFC North.” With the disagreement seemingly behind Coen and Saleh, the focus now shifts to what their teams do on the field on Sunday. The Titans enter Week 10 at 1-7 and sit at the bottom of the AFC South. They rank 29th with a PFN Offense Impact Score of 66.1. Jacksonvill

item.title: How Peoria-area girls swimmers and divers fared in the 2026 IHSA state finals prelims
item.description: Three Peoria-area swimmers advanced from the preliminary round of the 2026 Illinois High School Association girls swimming and diving state finals on Friday at the FMC Natatorium in Westmont. Peoria Notre Dame sophomore Kamryn Gardiner will swim in a pair of events, clocking the fastest time in the 100-yard butterfly (54.22 seconds) and the fifth-best in the 200-yard individual medley (2 minutes, 2.79 seconds). She'll be joined on the final day of the season by LaSalle-Peru co-op senior Samantha Nauman, who swam a 2:04.22 in the 200 IM. Nauman posted the second-fastest time in the 100-yard backstroke (54.47 seconds), while Washington co-op senior Maya Happel is in the 100-yard freestyle finals with the 16th-fastest time of 52.43 seconds. Each preliminary event sends the top 16 finishers to the finals. The top eight will compete in the "A" final, while the next eight placers are in the "B" final. All 16 places will earn state medals. Washington senior Ava Gensler will also compete Saturday in three events for athletes with disabilities — the 200-yard freestyle, the 50-yard freestyle and the 100-yard freestyle. In total, six relays, 10 individual swimmers and one diver in 15 events had qualified for state from the sectional level. item.title: Norman Powell reveals how Bulls overcame Hawks for OT win
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Matt Marton-Imagn Images Norman Powell reveals how Bulls overcame Hawks for OT win appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Chicago Bulls needed something to feel good about as they faced the Atlanta Hawks on Friday. They lost Caleb Wilson to a broken hand and fell into an eight-game losing streak. But the Bulls turned their pain into power and beat the Hawks in overtime, 125-117. Veteran guard Norman Powell , who came off back spasms, attributed one key element to their victory, per K.C. Johnson of The Chicago Sports Network. “Everybody was focused,” Powell said. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) "Everybody was focused." @KCJHoop with Norman Powell after the OT win: pic.twitter.com/GbaRgBNAu1 — Bulls on CHSN (@CHSN_Bulls) November 14, 2026 Powell started and finished with a game-high 33 points, shooting 12-for-19 from the field. Additionally, Powell was 4-for-8 from the 3-point line. But Powell wasn’t alone. Josh Giddey, Jalen Smith, and Isaac Okoro each finished with 15 points. In overtime, Smith was taken out after a hard fall in which he appeared to injure his hand. Giddey finished with a triple-double, with 14 assists and 10 rebounds. Additionally, Patrick Williams came off the bench and added 13 points. Buddy Hield, who surpassed Kyle Lowry on the 3-point list, finished with 12 points. Matas Buzelis walked away with 11 points and six rebounds. Moreover, Buzelis and Giddey combined for six turnovers, a far cry from the 13 they accumulated collectively against the San Antonio Spurs on Wednesday. As a result, the Bulls are now 2-9 and are about to embark on a road trip. On Saturday, they will play the Minnesota Timberwolves, the Cleveland Cavaliers on Monday, and then the Brooklyn Nets next Wednesday. Their next two home games will be next Friday, November 20, against the Washington Wizards, followed by the Denver Nuggets on Sunday, November 22. Related: Jalen Smith exits overtime game against Hawks after hard fall Related: Buddy Hield passes Kyle Lowry on all-time 3-point list

item.title: UCLA QB Ty Dieffenbach exits Illinois clash with shoulder injury, Madden Iamaleava takes over
item.description: Gary A. Vasquez-Imagn Images UCLA QB Ty Dieffenbach exits Illinois clash with shoulder injury, Madden Iamaleava takes over appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The U CLA football team may be 9-0 , but the Bruins are now down to their third string quarterback as Ty Dieffenbach had to be helped off the field in their game against the Illinois Fighting Illini. With less than a minute left in the second quarter and UCLA leading 10-0, Dieffenbach fell to the ground after attempting a pass. He clearly looked to be in discomfort as he held his left shoulder . Ty Dieffenbach is holding is shoulder after the play pic.twitter.com/Iq9dRmaUeC Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — wok (@wokdior) November 14, 2026 The Bruins were already without starting quarterback Nico Iamaleava, who went down with a season-ending left knee injury in last month’s win over Oregon . And now, Nico’s brother Madden has taken over at quarterback in the second half after Dieffenbach’s injury. Dieffenbach has done a fine job during his time as the Bruins’ starter. While his numbers (57.8% completion for 986 yards with six touchdowns and two interceptions heading into the Illinois game) have been unspectacular, he’s done enough to get the job done. He had a remarkable game last time out as he threw for 303 yards with three touchdowns despite just eight completions in a 34-20 win over Minnesota. It remains to be seen just how serious Dieffenbach’s shoulder injury is. But if it is significant and causes him to miss time, it will be another major setback for the Bruins and their hopes of making noise in the College Football Playoff. While the outstanding defense has been the big factor in their undefeated record, they still need some solid quarterback play to compete against the best teams in the country. That responsibility may now have to fall on the sophomore Madden Iamaleava’s young shoulders. Related: BYU’s clash with Baylor moved back after travel troubles Related: Utah clash with Arizona moved back 3 hours after canceling Friday’s flight

item.title: 2026 GM Meetings Recap
item.description: LAS VEGAS, NV - NOVEMBER 11: Rollie Fingers greets William Contreras during the 2026 MLB Awards presented by MGM Rewards at The Chelsea at The Cosmopolitan of Las Vegas on Wednesday, November 11, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Matt Aguirre/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images This week, the GM Meetings took place in Las Vegas. It is the first real chance for GMs to meet and discuss trade possibilities with other teams, as well as hold initial meetings with free agents. It was also awards week for MLB, with the yearly awards all announced. Here’s what took place this week. There wasn’t much for free agent deals, but a few were signed this week to kick off free agency. The big news for the Brewers was Jake Bauers signing with the Red Sox , which also means that he turned down the qualifying offer from Milwaukee. Bauers signed a four year, $58 million contract with the Red Sox, and the Brewers will receive a compensatory draft pick after the first round. A couple of other free agents were signed at the meetings, with Emilio Pagan signing with the Tigers and Evan Phillips signing with the Braves. Another piece of news for the Brewers was about Jeferson Quero. The Brewers were officially granted a fourth option year for Quero , meaning they can keep him in the minors for one more year. Without the option, Quero would either have to make the roster out of spring training or potentially be exposed to waivers to keep in the minors. Now, the Brewers can give him one more season in Nashville to see what he can offer in the future. Early trade rumors are coming up for current Brewers’ players, mainly focused around the players who are free agents after the 2027 season. The main two players that have been mentioned in rumors so far are Trevor Megill and William Contreras. At the meetings, Matt Arnold spoke about the possibility of trading Contreras . He did it with usual GM speak, saying that Contreras “means a lot to this team”. When asked about Megill, he continued with the GM speak and said, “He got the last six outs of the World Series, and I just went to a Metallica concert with him, so I like him. I like him a lot.” The yearly awards were also announced at this year’s meetings, and as expected for the World Series champions, they were represented several times. Here is a summary of the awards that they won or received votes for: Logan Henderson finished sixth in the NL Rookie of the Year vote, with Sal Stewart of the Reds and Kevin McGonigle of the Tigers taking the award . Manager Pat Murphy won his third straight NL Manager of the Year award , while Will Venable of the White Sox won it in the AL. Jacob Misiorowski was a unanimous winner of the NL Cy Young award , with Cam Schlitter also a unanimous winner in the AL. Trevor Megill finished third in the inaugural Reliever of the Year award, with Mason Miller taking the award in the NL and Louis Varland in the AL. Aaron Ashby and Abner Uribe also received votes. Brice Turang

item.title: Canada embrace Concacaf experience in win over Guatemala
item.description: Canada embrace Concacaf experience in win over Guatemala By Ben Steiner A fireworks-filled anthem, a less-than-ideal playing surface, and cages surrounding the pitch. Away days in Concacaf aren’t for the faint of heart, but Canada scraped out a 3-2 win over Guatemala on Friday. Under head coach Jesse Marsch, Canada have faced some of the world's best teams and reached the FIFA World Cup Round of 16. Yet Friday's opening 45 minutes of the Concacaf Nations League quarterfinals may have been among their most complete, before a disheartening second half saw a 3-0 lead nearly disappear. Jonathan David brought his stellar LaLiga form to the Estadio El Trébol, posting 1g/1a and helping build up Canada’s third goal. Liam Millar, in dominant form in the EFL Championship, scored too, while former Minnesota United striker Tani Oluwaseyi netted his first for Canada in 18 appearances. “We were very happy with that start,” assistant coach Mauro Biello told reporters, taking media duties after Marsch’s second-half red card. “It was something that we addressed here in the build-up to be able to create more, to score more goals, and I think we're very happy with the way our forwards played. Especially in the first half, and getting goals from both strikers and Liam, who was also doing really well at his club.” Alphonso Davies blow It had been more than 600 days since Alphonso Davies last started for Canada, when he tore his ACL in the 2025 Nations League third-place game against the United States . It seemed as if his return, committing to playing for Les Rouges on a November night in Guatemala amid stellar FC Bayern Munich form, was him putting the last two years of injury troubles behind him. That hope lasted just five minutes before an awkward shot block sent him off the pitch early. As of Friday, it was unclear if Davies would be available for the pivotal second leg in Canada or fly back to Germany to recover. His team’s first-half response, though, spoke volumes about the development beyond the 26-year-old’s contributions. “We were all so excited to see Phonzie back, and for him to go down that early, we were just gutted for him,” Oluwaseyi said. “We still played a really good game, and we got a win in a really tough place. I think overall, this is just the mentality of the entire team.” Invaluable experience Despite the lackluster second half, Canada got a largely new experience playing in Friday’s environment, marking the program’s first game in Central America since 2022, when only five of the players who saw minutes Friday were on the roster against Honduras. For Real Salt Lake center back Luc De Fougerolles , it could prove pivotal, as he thrived in a commanding role for most of the night and showed veteran poise alongside Portland Timbers center back Joel Waterman among the starters. And for the new era of Canadian players, who have largely played at home, in the US or against Caribbean foes, a true Concacaf away day will be invaluable as they aim for

item.title: 'We need patience' - Argentina boss Lionel Scaloni backs young talents to bounce back after 2-1 Uruguay loss in post-Messi era opener
item.description: FBL-FRIENDLY-ARG-URU - AFP Argentina head coach Lionel Scaloni has called for patience with his emerging youngsters after the Albiceleste suffered a 2-1 friendly defeat against Uruguay at La Bombonera on Friday. Playing their first match since Lionel Messi retired from international football last month, the hosts could not overturn two quickfire second-half goals in Buenos Aires. Set-piece goals sink rebuilding hosts Scaloni's side began their new chapter without their 39-year-old icon in front of a sparse crowd, just days after the manager signed a four-year extension . Following a goalless opening period where Cristopher Fiermarin denied Julian Alvarez and Nico Paz, Diego Forlan's visitors struck twice from Giorgian de Arrascaeta set pieces via a Leonardo Balerdi own goal and Maxi Araujo's effort. Atletico Madrid striker Alvarez replied from Gianluca Prestianni's cross, but Uruguay held firm. Manager shields emerging attacking trio Speaking after the match , Scaloni stated: "It was a good performance, regardless of the final result; we played well in the second half. We have to rebuild without Leo Messi, and we have the talent to bounce back from this defeat. It gives me plenty to analyse. We nearly pinned Uruguay back in the second half. We knew it would be tough, and now we just have to keep working." Protecting his youngsters, he added: "We couldn't quite find the right moments for the young lads to play their natural game. We can't expect them to carry the team on their shoulders - it's tough, and their team-mates will help them through it. As for the fans, they'll come back to cheer us on, even though he's no longer here. It's up to us to spark that enthusiasm in the supporters." He explained: "You never plan to lose... Still, there are ways to lose. We had one clear-cut chance in the first half and several in the second. We didn't get our reward, and once things start clicking better for us, it will be easier for the youngsters like Nico Paz, Soule, and Prestianni. They need to find their rhythm in this shirt; it's difficult for them." On replacing Exequiel Palacios with Roma winger Matias Soule, he noted: "We didn't want to disrupt the team's structure too much. We made substitutions, and we'll keep experimenting. We looked for something different in the second half with Soule, which is why we took off Palacios. Matias actually came on and looked sharp, right before they hit us with two quick goals. The idea was to look for one-on-one situations down that flank, with Enzo and Alexis anchoring the midfield." Tactician defends stopper and keeper Comparing the game to usual home outings, Scaloni commented: "Opponents usually come here and sit back. Tonight, Uruguay came out to press and play. We need patience as a team and throughout this process, because the superstars aren't here anymore and you have to give good players time. Let's not expect the youngsters to decide matches on their own - hopefully that happens, but let's not put that b

item.title: Colts’ Defense Takes Crushing Hit Before Dolphins Game
item.description: JACKSONVILLE, FL - NOVEMBER 01: Tight End Nate Boerkircher #87 of the Jacksonville Jaguars makes a catch for a touchdown over Linebacker Jaylon Carlies #57 of the Indianapolis Colts during the first half of the game at EverBank Stadium on November 1, 2026 in Jacksonville, Florida. (Photo by Don Juan Moore/Getty Images) Getty The Indianapolis Colts will face the Miami Dolphins with holes at multiple levels of their defense. Their latest injury update also leaves the offense and special teams searching for answers, creating a difficult personnel challenge before Sunday’s game. Indianapolis ruled out six players, according to The Athletic ’s James Boyd. Linebackers Jaylon Carlies and Akeem Davis-Gaither will miss the matchup, along with defensive tackle Jerry Tillery. Tight end Mo Alie-Cox, long snapper Luke Rhodes and right tackle Jalen Travis are also unavailable. Carlies is dealing with a neck injury, while Davis-Gaither has a knee issue. Tillery will sit because of a calf injury. Those absences put particular pressure on the middle of Indianapolis’ defense. Losing two linebackers simultaneously limits the coaching staff’s flexibility. Tillery’s absence adds another complication up front, where the Colts must distribute his workload among their available defensive linemen. The Dolphins now have an opportunity to challenge those replacements. Indianapolis must prevent its injury problems from becoming a weakness Miami can repeatedly exploit. Colts’ Defensive Depth Faces Immediate Test The concern extends beyond simply filling three spots on the defensive depth chart. Indianapolis also needs enough available players to rotate, handle different packages and respond if another injury occurs. At linebacker, communication will be especially important. The Colts cannot afford confusion over assignments while adjusting to the losses of Carlies and Davis-Gaither. Miami can test that coordination through motion, misdirection and throws into the middle of the field. Tillery’s absence could make that job harder. Defensive linemen help keep blockers away from linebackers, allowing them to pursue the ball. Indianapolis needs its remaining options to hold up without asking the players behind them to compensate for repeated breakdowns. That does not guarantee a productive afternoon for Miami. However, it gives the Colts less room for mistakes. The available defenders have an opportunity to earn additional trust. A strong performance could help their cases for larger roles beyond this matchup. First, Indianapolis needs them to execute against an opponent that can study exactly where the lineup has changed. Indianapolis Also Loses Offensive and Special Teams Pieces The defensive injuries account for only half of Indianapolis’ six-player list. Alie-Cox will miss the game with a groin injury. His absence removes an experienced tight end who can contribute as a blocker and receiving option. The Colts must cover those responsibilities through their remaining personnel

item.title: Ratliff, tenacious 'D' send New Lexington into regional final
item.description: NEW LEXINGTON - Lane Ratliff and a tenacious defense were enough for New Lexington on Friday night. Ratliff threw the game-winning touchdown and the defense made enough stands to send the second-seeded Panthers past third seed West Holmes 36-30 in the Division IV, Region 15 semifinal at Jim Rockwell Stadium. New Lexington (11-1) gets another rematch with top seed Indian Valley in the regional final next week. The Braves have won the last two meetings in the regional final, as the site for that will be announced on Sunday, Nov. 15. "Resiliency and perseverance. This group has been in this game for three straight years and knew what to expect," New Lex coach Kevin Board said. "Our defense stood tall at the right times. Tanner Toth set the table for that side of the ball, but we had a lot of guys make plays." Unified group | New Lex football's seniors are a 'special' blend of personalities 2026 wrap | Sheridan football didn't let setbacks ruin its season. What's next? As for the Knights, missed opportunities were their undoing. West Holmes had four drives end on turnover on downs in New Lex territory, including the final one that saw West Holmes drop a wide-open pass inside the New Lex 20. "We didn't capitalize on our opportunities," West Holmes coach Keaton Leppla said. "We've been aggressive all season, but we didn't come up with plays when we had chances to make them. That proved to be the difference." The game was tied at 14 at the half, and the Knights took a 27-22 lead entering the fourth after a 19-yard scoring run by Christopher Williams with 2:33 left in the third. The Panthers grabbed the lead about 90 seconds into the fourth when Ratliff scored from 2 yards out. The two-point run failed, but New Lex led 28-27, as a facemask penalty on West Holmes' aided that drive. The New Lex defense then made a timely stand. West Holmes had first-and-goal from the New Lex 9, but the Knights settled for a 23-yard field goal by Garrett Obrst for a 30-28 lead with 6:47 remaining in the game. Ratliff and New Lex needed little time to answer. A short kickoff aided the drive, which saw Ratliff find Tyson Spicer down the middle of the field for the go-ahead 41-yard touchdown. The two-point pass made it 36-30. West Holmes crossed into New Lex territory, but the defense made the stop. Ratliff and the offense then ran out the clock. "We faced a lot of adversity, and their offense was in good field position all game. We allowed them to have some long possessions, but we kept them out of the end zone just enough," New Lex's Eli Stephens said. "Our offense leaned on our line late in the game. Lane made some plays with his arm and his legs. It's what he does for us." Board applauded the offensive line, anchored by Stephens, and fellow seniors, Alberto Boggess and Bodie Decore. Hayden Finley and Carter Danison also held up on the right side, as New Lex willed its way to victory. "Our offensive line played great, especially in the second half," Board said. "They set th

item.title: Jonathan Law tops Lyman Hall on Witteman-to-Moulton TD pass with 56.8 seconds left
item.description: Hunter Kendzierski caught six passes for 169 yards and a touchdown in Law's 24-21 win over Lyman Hall on Friday, Nov. 13, 2026, in Wallingford. (Mike Madera/For Hearst Connecticut Media) WALLINGFORD - When the calendar shifts to the middle of November, all eyes shift to seeding and playoff implications throughout the state. Both the Jonathan Law and Lyman Hall football teams were well aware of what was at stake when the two squared off Friday evening in Wallingford. In an instant classic, Matt Witteman scrambled and found Reid Moulton for a 12-yard touchdown pass with 56.8 seconds remaining in the fourth quarter, giving Law a 24-21 win over Lyman Hall. With 56.8 seconds left Matt Witteman connected with Reid Moulton for a 12-yard TD to lead Law to a 24-21 win over Lyman Hall. Witteman threw for 2 TDs and rushed for another TD and Hunter Kendzierski caught six passes for 169 yards and a touchdown in Law's win. #cthsfb #connecticut #highschoolfootball (Pete Paguaga/Hearst Connecticut Media) "We have faith in our offense that we can score at any time," Law coach Ryan Pearson said. "It was a learning moment for us. We scored a little too quick against Xavier, and it came back to hurt us. This one we knew we had to march down the field and kill the clock because that offense over there is explosive. We did not want to give them too much time back on the clock." The two teams combined for 902 yards of offense, including 479 yards by the Trojans in the loss. Lyman Hall quarterback Ryan Casey ran for 193 yards in the loss. Trailing 21-17 after Lyman Hall scored on an 8-yard touchdown pass from Logan Michaels to Brent Michaud with 5:13 to go, Law marched 69 yards in 10 plays on the game-winning drive. Lyman Hall had one final opportunity, but the Law defense came up big, denying quarterback Ryan Casey and the Trojans. The first half saw a combined 506 yards and 24 points with Law leading 17-7 at the intermission. Witteman not only ran for 40 yards and a touchdown in the half, but he threw for 192 yards and a score for 232 of Law's 264 first-half yards. The Law defense was equally impressive in terms of keeping the high-powered Trojans out of the end zone. Lyman Hall had 242 yards of offense in the opening half, but managed only a 67-yard touchdown run by Michaud for a 7-3 lead with 2:27 left in the opening quarter, one offensive play after Law's Aiden Ramos kicked a 29-yard field goal. Witteman then took over for Law as he hit Hunter Kendzierski with a 74-yard scoring strike for a 10-7 lead with 9:57 left in the half. "It's fun," Kendzierski said. "I love getting the ball, seeing my teammates get the ball. These are big games." After the Law defense forced a punt, Witteman capped a 7-play, 54-yard drive with a 4-yard score and a 17-7 lead with 3:51 left in the half. Law's defense came up big in the final seconds of the first half, stopping Lyman Hall's Casey at the Law 3-yard line as time expired in the first half. Lyman Hall took the second-half kickoff

item.title: Duke Crushes SIUE, 90-47
item.description: DURHAM, NORTH CAROLINA - NOVEMBER 13: Joaquim Boumtje Boumtje #30 of the Duke Blue Devils defends in the second half against the SIU Edwardsville Cougars at Cameron Indoor Stadium on November 13, 2026 in Durham, North Carolina. (Photo by Lance King/Getty Images) | Getty Images D uke started slow against Southern Illinois University-Edwardsville, missing nine of its first 11 shots, before things got going. Duke controlled the boards early though, and got off to an early, if slow lead, at 6-2. Then the team just took off, going on a 25-6 run, behind a pair of threes from Caleb Foster, and an 11-0 burst, en route to a 90-47 win. SIUE fouled a lot early, putting Duke in the bonus in the first five minutes. Duke’s immense size advantage, paired with solid perimeter defense that held SIUE to 0-7 from behind the line, helped the Blue Devils roll out to a 43-20 lead. The second half was more of the same. SIUE hit a pair of threes early in the half, but there just wasn’t much the Cougars could do. Duke’s size and athleticism were overwhelming. The Blue Devils ripped off a closing run of 20-3, outscored SIUE 47-27 after the break, and ultimately won by 43. It was a lot better than we saw from Duke against Michigan State. Duke was much more aggressive and connected than they were in Chicago. The Blue Devils were more physical and aggressive on defense. Duke forced 19 turnovers, had 11 steals, and blocked eight shots. Five were by Patrick Ngongba; the other three were by Cameron Williams, who had his best game by far. SIUE shot about 14 percent from outside and 30 percent overall. Offensively, after the slow start, Duke shot 9-29 from outside (31 percent) and 30-66 overall (45 percent). If you deduct the cold 2-11 start, the Blue Devils shot 50.9 percent overall and 36 percent from behind the line. Inside, after the cold opening, Duke shot 63.3 percent. Ngongba, who looked healthy after playing somewhat sick against Michigan State, finished with 13 points on 4-6 shooting. He also had nine rebounds and four assists. JoJo Boumtje Boumtje finished with 11 points on 5-8/1-2 from the floor, and matched Ngongba on the boards with nine of his own. Dame Sarr finished with 12 points, four rebounds, and three assists. Cayden Boozer had 11 points, led the team in rebounding (!) with 10. He also had four assists. John Blackwell continued his recent offensive struggle with just three points, shooting 1-7. Caleb Foster came off the bench for 12 points and three boards. Sebastian Wilkins shot 1-5 from the floor, but hit 9-10 from the foul line. Williams finished with nine points. Coach Jon Scheyer said this about Duke’s offensive struggles: “Offensively, I thought we looked disjointed. We’re a little bit behind in role identification right now — knowing the strengths of each guy and how to position them the right way. As a coaching staff, we got to take the next step with that to help our team.” With high-powered Illinois in Cameron on Tuesday, figuring that out would be a

item.title: Thunder’s Isaiah Hartenstein, Nikola Topic connect for textbook alley-oop dunk vs. Clippers
item.description: Thomas Shea-Imagn Images Thunder’s Isaiah Hartenstein, Nikola Topic connect for textbook alley-oop dunk vs. Clippers appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Oklahoma City Thunder visited the Los Angeles Clippers at Intuit Dome in the NBA Cup on Friday, hoping to end a two-game skid suffered at the hands of the Portland Trail Blazers . The Thunder have been hobbled by major injuries to Jalen Williams, Chet Holmgren, and Cason Wallace, and everyone needs to step up to get back on track. Nikola Topic made his season debut against the Clippers. He immediately made a good play in the first quarter, driving to the lane and attracting the defense before making the perfect lob to Isaiah Hartenstein for the easy dunk . Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Nikola Topić throws a PERFECT LOB, and Isaiah Hartenstein slams it home 💥 pic.twitter.com/q4TCbavxYm — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) November 14, 2026 Topic has always been a gifted passer, but he has struggled to get his career going. Drafted by Oklahoma City with the No. 12 pick in 2024, he missed his rookie year due to an ACL injury. Last year, he was diagnosed with testicular cancer, limiting him to just 10 games. Hartenstein, for his part, has been consistently solid , filling the void left by Holmgren in the frontcourt. Entering the game against the Clippers, he was averaging 8.0 points, 10.1 rebounds, 3.7 assists, and 1.2 steals. The 21-year-old Topic could see more action with Ajay Mitchell still sidelined by an ankle sprain. While the Thunder have played well despite their depleted roster, a collective effort is needed to sustain their strong showing. Coach Mark Daigneault has preached about having a next-man-up mentality to help Shai Gilgeous-Alexander amid their challenging stretch. As of this writing, the Thunder are trailing the Clippers in the second quarter. Hartenstein has six points, three rebounds, and two assists, while Topic has three rebounds, two assists, and one steal. item.title: Caldwell football sweeps Richwood in first playoff win in three years
item.description: COLUMBIA — For the first time since 2023, Caldwell's football team has won an LHSAA postseason game. The Spartans saw a familiar opponent in Richwood as the two teams played each other in the Division III nonselect first round for the third time in four seasons. The Rams defeated Caldwell in last fall's playoffs, but the Spartans also bested Richwood in 2023 and pitched a shutout earlier this season as well. Behind three rushing touchdowns from junior quarterback Bridger McCann and the defense forcing key takeaways in the second half, Caldwell completed the season sweep against Richwood with its 30-12 victory on Friday, Nov. 13, at Spartan Stadium. "I'm just excited for the boys," Caldwell coach Cleo Head said. "Anytime you play a team twice, and a team as athletic as Richwood is, they can score quick. The defense played hard. They continued to fight all night long, and my kids just never laid down." LHSAA football: Every first-round score involving the Monroe area Caldwell (9-2) has been one of northeast Louisiana's hottest teams with five straight victories. It's won twice as many games this fall than it has the last two seasons combined. The Spartans' only losses of the season, against Mangham and Union Parish, were decided by one possession. Some of Caldwell's biggest victories were its season opener against Grant and its 14-point fourth quarter comeback three weeks ago against Oak Grove. "I would say as a brotherhood, we've gotten closer," McCann said on Caldwell's growth. "Those past years, we weren't quite together and connected as we were. This year, I think everybody on the team is playing for one goal, and that's playing for each other to win." After playing running back, McCann is continuing to step up in his first year as starting quarterback. In addition to his three rushing touchdowns against Richwood (5-6), he threw the game-winning touchdown pass to sophomore Jahari Stanley to beat Oak Grove. "I knew I was going to take on the job of running the ball a lot," Bridger said of his new role. "(Against Richwood) with the weather, I didn't pass that (well), but I was able to use my running back abilities to get the job done." "Anytime the coaches challenge him, or he has a challenge in the game, he just keeps on stepping up," sophomore Blayne Dunn said. "He does everything in his ability to move the ball downfield and score and command his offense well." Richwood got on the board late in the game as senior Jarvis Walker connected with junior Christopher Qualls. Walker then threw his second touchdown pass of the evening to sophomore Pooh Pollard but was intercepted on the Rams' prior drive by junior Lander McCann. "I was expanding to the flats more and reading the quarterback's eyes and trust what my coaches teaches me to do," Lander McCann said of the interception. item.title: Taking care of business among key Rangers takeaways in convincing win over Canucks
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Plain and simple, the New York Rangers took care of business Friday night in Vancouver, overwhelming the last-place Canucks 5-1 at Rogers Arena. Which is exactly what should have been expected. Make no mistake, this is a game the Rangers (12-8-1) had to have. Not only to ensure a winning road trip in the Pacific Northwest, but because the Canucks (3-17-1) are an absolute train wreck, the worst team by far in the NHL. Though the Rangers started slowly in the first period, there was only one expected and acceptable outcome. And that was a Rangers victory. No excuses. Yes, the Canucks are that bad. They’ve now lost seven in a row, and have just one victory in their past 18 games (1-16-1) since Oct. 4 after winning two of their first three. They’re the worst defensive team in the League , allowing more than four and a half goals per game on average, and their penalty kill is simply atrocious. So, even though the Canucks took a 1-0 on an Elias Pettersson deflection at 12:13 of the first period, and the Rangers hadn’t won a game this season after giving up the first goal, there was no way visitors could lose this game. And they didn’t. Gabe Perreault ‘s short-side snipe at 18:47 of the first tied things up. And then it was a master class by the Rangers in the second period. They scored four unanswered goals in a span of 7:49, out-shot the Canucks 12-4, and had a whopping expected goal share 5v5 of 84.02 percent, per Natural Stat Trick . Through two periods, the Rangers had a 16-6 advantage in high-danger chances. They took their foot off the gas some in the third period, but Dylan Garand stopped all 13 shots he faced in the final frame. New York was the far better team at even strength, and on special teams — where they scored once on teh power play and were a perfect 3-for=3 on the penalty kill. Though none of this should come as a surprise. The Rangers took three of four on this road trip, after beginning it with just one road victory on the season. And this latest victory represented their first in nine games when allowing the first goal (1-7-1).4 They reach the season’s quarter-mark third in the Metropolitan Division, and winners in five of their past six games. And without a bitter taste in their collective mouth if they hadn’t taken care of business in a can’t-lose game in Vancouver. Key takeways after Rangers throttle last-place Canucks 5-1 Bob Frid-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Happy homecoming It was a very happy homecoming for two BC boys — and by that we mean British Columbia, not Boston College, Perreault’s goal notwithstanding. Glenn Gawdin scored the first two goals of his NHL career, and the Richmond, BC native did so in his first-ever game in Vancouver. Playing his second game since he was recalled from Hartford of the American Hockey League to center New York’s fourth line earlier in the week, the 29-year-old took full advantage of a terrible giveaway by Canucks goalie Leevi Meri

item.title: ‘Random Quentin Grimes Stray,’ ‘This Has to Be Fake’ – WNBA Fans Baffled Over Sophie Cunningham’s Response to Luka Dončić Comparison
item.description: Collage featuring Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham (8) celebrates a 3-pointer Sunday, Sept. 27, 2026, during the first half of Game 1 of the and BASKETBALL-NBA-MIL-LAL/. USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect / IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect On Thursday’s episode of the “No Hesitation” podcast, Drew Hanlen compared Los Angeles Lakers superstar Luka Dončić’s first nine games of the 2026-27 NBA season with Sophie Cunningham’s entire 2026 WNBA campaign. The answer he got back left fans in disbelief, as Indiana Fever guard Cunningham turned the conversation to the gap between their paychecks and pulled another Lakers guard into the mix. Fans React as Sophie Cunningham’s Response to Luka Dončić Comparison Ropes In Quentin Grimes Hanlen, who trains Boston Celtics star Jayson Tatum, compared Dončić’s shot and free-throw attempts with Cunningham’s 2026 totals: “Through his first nine games, he has attempted 221 shots. You, last season in 43 games, attempted 226 shots. Luka has attempted 102 free throws already after nine games. Last season, you attempted 74.” Cunningham answered , “You’re missing a big one. He also makes $50 million a year. I make $700,000 on my WNBA check. You should compare me more to Quentin Grimes. You know, we average around, you know, eight to 10 points. … My 3-point shooting is actually better than both of them. And so if we’re going to compare, let’s compare.” Grimes had no part in Hanlen’s setup, and his sudden spot in the conversation drew a laugh from one fan, who called it a “Random Quentin Grimes stray.” As for the paychecks, Cunningham signed a one-year, $665,000 deal with the Fever for 2026, up from the $100,000 she made in 2025. Dončić is earning $49.5 million this season under a three-year, $165 million extension. In scoring, Cunningham and Grimes are a tenth of a point apart, with Cunningham averaging 7.9 points in 2026 and Grimes at 8.0 for the Lakers this season. Another hoops fan kept the spotlight on the Lakers guard, writing “Quentin Grimes in the mud.” Grimes was not the only part of the answer that drew a reaction, as one fan was puzzled and wrote : “I’ve never seen her in her bag like this, what are we talkin’ about here smh.” Another fan reacted with plain disbelief, remarking , “This has to be fake.” The 3-point claim at the end of her answer drew its own skepticism, as one fan posted, “Not watching the clip but she said she shoots better than Luka and QG? C’mon man, what we doin’.” However, Cunningham’s claim does hold up against the current shooting percentages. She converted 41.9% of her 3-point attempts during the 2026 WNBA season, compared with Dončić’s 40.8% and Grimes’ 24.2% through the current season. Though the Fever star’s hot take continues to stir up debate, Cunningham’s and Dončić’s roles are far apart. item.title: 4 Reasons Why The Spurs Were So Dominant Against Warriors In 123-85 Victory
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Daniel Dunn-Imagn Images The San Antonio Spurs had one of their most convincing performances of the season, dismantling the Golden State Warriors 123-85 in a game that was decided well before the final buzzer. Victor Wembanyama controlled the interior and had his MVP-level two-way play shine. Stephon Castle orchestrated the offense, and San Antonio overwhelmed Golden State with its combination of size, athleticism, and defensive intensity. The Spurs finished with a massive 60-43 rebounding advantage, scored 56 points in the paint, and recorded 34 assists while holding the Warriors to just 33.3% shooting from the field . Golden State never led, and San Antonio’s largest advantage reached 43 points. Here are four reasons why the Spurs were so dominant against the Warriors. 1. Stephon Castle Had A Brilliant 32-Point Performance Stephon Castle was arguably the biggest offensive difference-maker in this matchup. The Spurs guard finished with 32 points on 12-18 shooting, including five three-pointers on eight attempts. He also contributed six assists, five rebounds, and a block while committing just one turnover. Castle’s efficiency was particularly impressive considering how much responsibility he carried offensively. He consistently converted his opportunities while helping San Antonio maintain its offensive rhythm. His performance complemented the Spurs’ interior dominance perfectly. Golden State had no reliable answer for Castle’s scoring, and his ability to create offense helped San Antonio establish an overwhelming advantage early. 2. Victor Wembanyama Dominated The Interior Wembanyama didn’t need an enormous scoring performance to completely influence the game. The Spurs superstar finished with 12 points, 12 rebounds, six assists, two steals, and two blocks in just 21 minutes. His defensive presence helped San Antonio control the paint while his passing contributed to the team’s impressive offensive movement. Golden State scored only 28 points in the paint, compared to San Antonio’s 56. That 28-point difference illustrates just how thoroughly the Spurs controlled the interior. Wembanyama’s combination of rim protection, rebounding, and playmaking made him an enormous advantage even without a high-volume scoring night. 3. San Antonio’s Ball Movement Completely Outclassed Golden State The Spurs played exceptionally unselfish basketball. San Antonio recorded 34 assists on 46 made field goals, demonstrating how effectively the team generated quality scoring opportunities. Golden State finished with just 23 assists on 31 made shots. The difference extended beyond passing numbers. San Antonio shot 48.4% from the field, while Golden State struggled to convert just 33.3% of its attempts. Devin Vassell, De’Aaron Fox, Dylan Harper, and Castle all contributed to the offensive structure, while Harrison Barnes and Keldon Johnson provided additional production off the bench. item.title: Rockwall fends off Wylie comeback for bi-district playoff win
item.description: Rockwall quarterback Collins Jones (8) high-fives Rockwall wide receiver Brayden Puffer (1) after a touchdown during the first half of a Class 6A Division I bi-district playoff game at Wilkerson-Sanders Memorial Stadium, Friday, Nov. 13, 2026 in Rockwall. (Chris Swann/The Dallas Morning News) ROCKWALL — Last season, Rockwall missed the playoffs for the first time in over 10 years. Friday night, the team put its frustrations to rest in a 66-48 bi-district round win that wasn’t as close as the final score indicates. Rockwall wide receiver Ryan Wiley (17) is brought down by Wylie defensive back Chetachi Nwokedi (7) during the first half of a Class 6A Division I bi-district playoff game at Wilkerson-Sanders Memorial Stadium, Friday, Nov. 13, 2026 in Rockwall. (Chris Swann/The Dallas Morning News) After Wylie’s Ohio State-pledge running back, Daylon Gordon, returned the kickoff 77 yards to set up the team’s opening touchdown, Rockwall opened a 14-7 lead on a 20-yard touchdown run from senior running back Kaydon Castro. The team went for an onside kick on the ensuing kickoff and recovered it, driving the field again in six plays for another 20-yard touchdown by Castro, on a pass from quarterback Collins Jones, to take a two-score lead. Related: Click here for the full box score and play-by-play On the final drive of the first quarter, after Rockwall had consistently run the ball with Castro up to that point, Collins Jones pulled the read option and broke a 47-yard touchdown to make it 28-7. Rockwall went on a 28-0 scoring run that ended with a 49-yard touchdown catch by Kendall Johnson as the halftime horn blew. What looked like a back-and-forth affair for the first five minutes had turned into a rout. “I felt great about the way that we played, just pedal to the metal in the first half,” Rockwall head coach Trey Brooks said. “A little bit of a weird second half. But I’m proud of the way that our guys played. It’s what we needed to do.” Brooks said the program not only missing the postseason in 2025, but also suffering its first losing season since 2012, lit a fire under the team this offseason to get back to the standard of winning Rockwall was used to. “This is where we belong,” Brooks said. “It’s been a long stretch of really good football for Rockwall, and I just feel like last year was just a little bump in the road, and we’re back where we need to be.” Rockwall opened the second half with a 36-yard touchdown run from Alijha Deloache to make it 56-7. Deloache finished with a team-high 96 yards and a touchdown. Wylie added six touchdowns in the second half in a late comeback effort, but Rockwall added one more touchdown pass in the fourth quarter from Jones to Logan Shouse to ice the victory.
